name: Press Break
idea: When the other team guards the whole court, pass the ball to the middle, then pass it ahead before they can trap you.
why: A press wants you to dribble into a trap. But passes are faster than any defender. A pass to the middle leaves the trap behind the ball, and a pass ahead finds teammates running free, often with more players than the defense has back.
tryit: Practice five against five on the whole court. The rule: never dribble into a trap. When you're trapped, pivot, stay calm, and look for the middle. Everyone else: come toward the ball or run ahead.

frames.say: Red just scored, so blue passes in from under red's hoop, at the far end of the court. Red is *pressing*: guarding the whole court so blue can't bring the ball up.
{1} cuts to the corner to get open, and {4} passes it in fast.
*Trap!* {X4} and {X1} trap {1} in the corner. {5} runs to the middle, right behind the trap, and {4} steps in to help.
*Pass to the middle!* {1} stays calm and passes over the trap to {5}. Now the trap is behind the ball!
{5} turns and passes ahead to {2}, racing up the side. A pass is faster than any defender.
{2} dribbles at the basket. {X3} is the only red player back and has to stop {2}, so {3} is all alone.
Two players against one defender: {2} passes to {3}.
Layup! Beat the press: get open, pass to the middle, then pass ahead.
